sections.english: Further, the rational soul traverses the whole universe and its surrounding void, explores the shape of it, stretches into the infinity of time, encompasses and comprehends the periodic regeneration of the Whole. It reflects that our successors will see nothing new, just as our predecessors saw nothing other than we see now: so that in a man of forty, with a modicum of intelligence, has seen, in a sense, all that was and ever will be — the constant sameness of things.
sections.chinese: 更进一步，理性之灵魂周游整个宇宙及其周遭之虚空，探索其形态，延入时间之无穷，环抱并领会那宇宙整体之周期新生。它深省到：后来者将看不到任何新物，正如已逝之众先人所见者亦不逾于吾人今日之所见；故在一个四十岁之人，只要稍具智识，便已在某种意义上见识过一切曾发生之事——也见识了一切将永来者——概皆事物之恒常不变。

sections.english: Particular qualities too of the rational soul are love of neighbour, truthfulness, integrity, no higher value than itself. This last is a defining quality of law also. There is thus no difference between the true principle of philosophy and the principle of justice.
sections.chinese: 理性灵魂之特别品质亦有：爱邻人、诚实、正直，及不以他物为高于己身者——此最后一端亦是法律之界定品质。故此，哲学之真原则与正义之原则之间，并无分别。

sections.english: You will think little of the entertainment of song or dance or all-in wrestling if you deconstruct the melodic line of a song into its individual notes and ask yourself of each of them: 'Is this something that overpowers me?' You will recoil from that admission. So too with a comparable analysis of dance.
sections.chinese: 若你将一支曲目之旋律线分解为单独逐个之音符，且于每一音符反躬自问：「这音符能征服我吗？」，你便会不以为然。你将悻悻然避之而耻对自己的坦承。以相似之分析去肢解舞蹈也是一样。

sections.english: What a noble thing is the soul ready for its release from the body, if now must be the time, and prepared for whatever follows — extinction, dispersal, or survival! But this readiness must come from a specific decision: not in mere revolt, like the Christians, but thoughtful, dignified, and — if others are to find you credible — without any air of tragedy.
sections.chinese: 灵魂若已备妥于一旦有需从其肉身得释之时——无论随后者为何物：灭绝、离散、或续存——这是一件何其高贵之事！但此等备妥，须从一种特定之决断中出来：不可仅在爆发般之叛逆中——并非那类出于一时之愤激——而是沉静、有尊严、且——若要令人信服——不带一丝悲剧表演之气。

sections.english: Have I done something for the common good? Then I too have benefited. Have this thought always ready to hand: and no stopping.
sections.chinese: 我可曾为公共之福祉做了什么事？若然，则我自身亦已受益。常备此念于心：然后不要休止。

sections.english: What is your profession? Being a good man. But this can only come about through philosophic concepts — concepts of the nature of the Whole, and concepts of the specific constitution of man.
sections.chinese: 你的职志为何？做一良善之人。但此仅能经由那些哲学之概念而成就——彼关乎宇宙整体本性及人之特定构造之概念方可达也。

sections.english: First, tragedies were brought on stage to remind you of what can happen, that these happenings are determined by nature, and that what moves you in the theatre should not burden you on the larger stage of life. You can see the way things must turn out and that even those who cry 'Oh Cithaeron!' must bear it.
sections.chinese: 首先，悲剧之搬上舞台，乃为提醒你何事可能发生，而这些事情皆由自然所注定——且在那戏院里所动你心的那点事情，不该在人生这更大的舞台上成为你之负担。你能看清万物必然归趋之道，且即便那些口中狂呼「呜呼喀泰戎！」的人，也必须忍受这一切。

sections.english: Just as those who try to block your progress along the straight path of reason will not be able to divert you from principled action, so you must not let them knock you out of your good will towards them. Rather you should watch yourself equally on both fronts, keeping not only a stability of judgement but also a calm response to those who try to thwart you in other ways. To be angry with them is no less a weakness than to abandon your course of action and be panicked into surrender.
sections.chinese: 正如那些妄图阻挡你在理性之正道上向前精进的人，终究不能将你从有原则之行动中拐开分毫——同样，你也不可让他们将你逐出你对他们的那份善意。倒是应当在两条阵线上同样审视自己，既要保持判断之安稳不动，也要保持对那些试图以其他方式挫败你者的平静回应。对他们发怒，同样是一软弱之举——正如放弃你之行动路线、因惊慌而屈服般无异。

sections.english: 'No nature is inferior to art': in fact the arts imitate the variety of natures. If that is so, then the most perfect and comprehensive of all natures could not be surpassed by any artistic invention. Now all arts create the lower in the interests of the higher: so this is the way of universal nature too. And from here is the origin of justice, which gives rise to all the other virtues. Justice cannot be maintained if we set value on things indifferent, or are easily deceived, or stumble at obstacles, or are subject to change.
sections.chinese: 「无一自然逊色于技艺」。事实上，诸门技艺所摹仿者，正是诸般自然之多姿样态。若果如此，则一切自然中之最完美且最涵盖者，断无任何人为手艺之发明可出其右。那么，一切技艺皆为更高者之利益而创造所低等者：故此，这也是宇宙本性所行之方式。正义正起源于此处——而正义又生发出一切其他之美德。正义若不能在行事时受到尊崇，便无可持守——不论我们是否执着地寄价值于那漠不相干之物，或轻易受欺，或在阻碍面前屡屡绊跌，或顺从于因果迁变之摆布——正义都将无法立足。

sections.english: The external things whose pursuit or avoidance troubles you do not force themselves on you, but in a way you yourself go out to them. However that may be, keep your judgement of them calm and they too will stay still — then you will not be seen either to pursue or to avoid.
sections.chinese: 那些你趋之若骛或避之唯恐不及而致烦乱你的外在事物，并非它们自己强加于你的——相反，在某种意义下，是你自己先走向了它们。然不论情况为何，只要保持你对此类物之判断于安然，它们自身亦将随之不动——如是，你便不显得像在追索，也不像在躲闪。

sections.english: The soul is a sphere which retains the integrity of its own form if it does not bulge or contract for anything, does not flare or subside, but keeps the constant light by which it sees the truth of all things and the truth in itself.
sections.chinese: 灵魂乃是一球体，若能不为任何事而凸鼓或挛缩，不燃出偏焰也不往下沉陷，而保持着那恒常之光芒——并以此光见照万物之真理与己内之真理——则此球即能持存其自身形式之完满。

sections.english: Someone despises me? That is his concern. But I will see to it that I am not found guilty of any word or action deserving contempt. Will he hate me? That is his concern. But I will be kind and well-intentioned to all, and ready to show this very person what he is failing to see — not in any criticism or ostentation, but in genuine good faith.
sections.chinese: 某人鄙视我？那是他的事。但我将留意于此：决不让自己被发现在任何一言一行之举上，该当配得起轻蔑。他将恨我吗？那也是他的事。但我将对一切人都仁善而怀好意，且甘愿示知此一具体之当事者他所忽略了而未看见的是什么——并非存心存意地表显出责备或炫示苛责，而是以真正由衷之信念身体力行。

sections.english: They despise each other, but still toady to each other: they want to win, but still grovel.
sections.chinese: 他们彼此鄙视，却又彼此谄媚迎合；他们想赢过对方，却仍旧卑躬屈膝趴伏在地。

sections.english: The rotten pretence of the man who says, 'I prefer to be honest with you'! What are you on about, man? No need for this preface — the reality will show. It should be written on your forehead, immediately clear in the tone of your voice and the light of your eyes, just as the loved one can immediately read all in his lover's glance. In short, the good and honest man should have the same stamp as the rank-smelling goat, so that whoever stands close must be aware of it, will he nill he. Calculated honesty is a stiletto.
sections.chinese: 那口中说「我这人，宁可和你掏心见胆」的家伙，是何等腐臭之伪饰！你嚼什么舌根呢，人啊？何须此前言引子——那事实就是会将你揭露。它当下就该刻在你之前额上，当下在你音声的音调和目光的清度上清清楚楚——就如所爱者可在其情人一瞥中尽读一切情愫那般。简而言之：那良善而正直之人，当有着如同浑身发出刺鼻异味之公羊一样的印记——不论谁无论他愿意与否，靠近他一站便必觉知。狡计裁夺过的一副坦诚，那可真是一把利小刀。

sections.english: Live through life in the best way you can. The power to do so is in a man's own soul, if he is indifferent to things indifferent. And he will be indifferent if he looks at these things both as a whole and analysed into their parts, and remembers that none of them imposes a judgement of itself or forces itself on us. These things stay still, while it is we who create the judgements about them, and inscribe them (so to speak) on ourselves, even though we need not inscribe them, or, if we do, we can erase them.
sections.chinese: 以你能达到的最善方式度此一生。这样的能力就在于一个人自家的灵魂里——若能不执于那些漠不相干之事物。而他于它们能做到淡然相看，便也须将此类事物视为整全、也将它们分解开来看成仔细分体来视察，并记取：其中并无任何一个是强加以它自身之判断给我们、或将自身硬塞到我们身上的。这些事物静止不动，乃是我们自己创造了关于它们的这些判断，又以某种方式书写、刻画在我们自己心里——尽管我们原本不必刻画上去；或者，即使未曾企及这般，也还是能够最终将它们擦除以去的。

sections.english: With each object of experience consider its origin, its constituents, what it is changing into, what it will be when changed — and that no harm will come to it.
sections.chinese: 面对每一经验之对象，思量其由来、其构成部分、它将变成什么、变化之后将成为何物——并知晓，并无伤害降临于它。

sections.english: First. How do I regard my relation to them, and the fact that we were all born for each other: and, turning the argument, that I was born to be their leader, as the ram leads his flock and the bull his herd? But start from first principles. If not atoms, then nature governing all: if so, then the lower are for the sake of the higher, and the higher for each other.
sections.chinese: 第一：我怎样看待我之于他们的关系，以及吾辈皆是为了彼此而出生这一事实；再换个角度说，我之被造乃为做他们的领头者——如公羊领其群，公牛统其兽群那般。不过，还是从头一项原则说起。既非原子，便是自然统御一切；若果如此，则低者乃为高者而有，而高者又彼此相为养惠。

sections.english: There are four particular corruptions of the directing mind for which you must keep constant watch, and eliminate them whenever you detect them. First: 'This mental image is superfluous.' Second: 'This could weaken the bond of community.' Third: 'This would not be yourself speaking to yourself.' Fourth: 'This is a violation of the divine element within you.'
sections.chinese: 主导之心灵有四桩特定之腐败偏差，你必须恒常警觉防范，并一经察觉便立时将其消除。其一：「这心中形象乃是不必要之多余。」其二：「这势将削弱那共同体的连结纽带。」其三：「此非你自己在对你自己讲的话。」其四：「这乃是亵渎你内中神性之份量。」

sections.english: 'The man without one and the same aim in life cannot himself stay one and the same throughout his life.' The maxim is incomplete unless you add what sort of aim that should be. Judgements vary of the whole range of various things taken by the majority to be goods in one way or another, but only one category of aim is acceptable to me: the social good, that is, the common good.
sections.chinese: 「那个在生命中无一恒常相同之目标的人，断不能自己在全此一生中保持一恒常相同之状态。」此一格言若不增入其所应属之目标类项，则是不完整的。意见纷纭，于大多数人以这些或那些各般方式视作好的事物之通范围莫不如此；然而，唯有一类目标在我看是可以接受的：社群的善，也即公共之善好。

sections.english: The hill mouse and the house mouse — and the frightened scurrying of the house mouse.
sections.chinese: 山上的野鼠与家中的室鼠——以及那屋中鼠的惊惶之蹿窜。

sections.english: Socrates used to call the popular beliefs 'bogies', things to frighten children with.
sections.chinese: 苏格拉底习惯将那些流行之信条称为「妖恫之怪」，不过用之以吓唬孩童罢了。

sections.english: At their festivals the Spartans would put seats for visitors in the shade, and sit themselves wherever they could.
sections.chinese: 在他们的节庆中，斯巴达人会把阴凉处之座位让予来访的客人们，而自己不拘何处随地落坐。

sections.english: Socrates to Perdiccas of Macedon, declining the invitation to visit him: 'to avoid dying the worst of deaths' — that is, the inability to return in kind benefits received.
sections.chinese: 苏格拉底致信马其顿之佩尔狄卡斯（辞其邀请访问）道：「只为避免那最糟糕之死法」——即不能以同样恩惠报答所已受之好处也。

sections.english: In Epicurean writings there is laid down the precept that one should continually keep in mind one of those who followed the path of virtue in earlier times.
sections.chinese: 在伊壁鸩鲁学派之著述中，有一训谕被规订明载：当令一己常恒铭念古代早期那些遵循美德之途的先行者中的一人在心。

sections.english: The Pythagoreans say, 'Look at the sky at dawn' — to remind ourselves of the constancy of those heavenly bodies, their perpetual round of their own duty, their order, their purity, and their nakedness. No star wears a veil.
sections.chinese: 毕达哥拉斯学派有名句：「日出之前看那诸天」——为提醒我们那些穹苍星宿之恒常不变、它们各安其职的永续运行、它们肃穆的秩序、其纯粹，以及其赤露无遮。无一星辰佩戴罗帏面纱。

sections.english: Think of Socrates in his underclothes when Xanthippe had gone out with his coat: and what he said to his friends retiring in embarrassment when they saw the state of his dress.
sections.chinese: 想想苏格拉底，当他的妻子将他的外套抱走外出之际，他自己仅穿着底衬内裳之时的情形罢；也再记他对其朋友们——当他们看到他衣装困窘之态便尴尬退避之时——所言之语。

sections.english: In writing and reading you must learn before you can teach. Yet more so in life.
sections.chinese: 书写读阅，你必须先自学会，然后才能教人。而人生，却更是如此。

sections.english: Only a madman looks for figs in winter: just as mad to hope for a child when the time of this gift is past.
sections.chinese: 惟狂者在冬日里寻无花果；同样疯狂若当那赐赠的时刻已然过去，还寄望守候一婴孩的降临。

sections.english: Epictetus used to say that when you kiss your child you should say to yourself: 'Tomorrow you may be dead.' But these are ominous words! 'No,' he replies, 'nothing is ominous which points to a natural process. Otherwise it would be ominous to speak of the corn being reaped.'
sections.chinese: 爱比克泰德常说，你在亲吻自己孩子时，当在心里悄语自道：「明之日你或许便会死去了。」此终属一家不祥之言。「非也，」他答道「任何指示向一自然之过程之语，皆非不祥的——否则言及庄稼谷穗收割之事，也当成了不祥之辞了。」

sections.english: Grapes unripe, ripened, raisined: all changes, not into nonexistence, but into not-yet existence.
sections.chinese: 葡萄未熟，然后变熟，变作葡萄干：变化皆是——并非走向虚无，而是走入那尚未存在的存在形态中。

sections.english: 'No thief can steal your will' — so Epictetus.
sections.chinese: 「窃贼无能盗走你的意志」——此为爱比克泰德之言。

sections.english: Another saying of his: 'We must discover an art of assent, and in the whole field of our impulses take care to ensure that each impulse is conditional, has a social purpose, and is proportionate to the value of its goal.'
sections.chinese: 爱比克泰德又有一言：「吾辈必须发现一门『同意之术』，并于冲动之整个场域中留心确保每一冲动皆带有条件预设、抱持一社会性目的、且与其目标之价值恰成对称均衡。」

sections.english: Again. 'So this is not a contest for a trivial prize: at issue is madness or sanity.'
sections.chinese: 复有言：「如此看来，这并非一场奖酬微薄之竞斗：较量之焦点乃在疯狂抑或明智之间。」

sections.english: Socrates used to question thus. 'What do you want to have? The souls of rational or irrational beings?' 'Rational.' 'What sort of rational beings? The pure or the lower?' 'The pure.' 'Why then don't you aim for that?' 'Because we have it.' 'Why then your fighting and disagreements?'
sections.chinese: 苏格拉底习惯如此发问答疑：「你想拥有怎样的灵魂？理性存在者的，还是非理性的？」「理性的。」「哪一类的理性者？那纯洁的，还是那低劣的？」「纯洁的。」「如此，你缘何不追求此目标呢？」「因我们已拥有它了。」「既如此，你又为何而纷争不解与彼此龃龉呢？」
